ticket.title: Downstream projects cannot install the miter whose gates they document: published crates lag their tags, and a git install cannot resolve a cross-repo path dependency
ticket.description:
MEASURED 2026-11-12 from a downstream consumer (aerofoil), while making the suite gates run in CI (their AF-19).

THE VERSION LAG
  miter-cli 0.1.0-beta.4 on crates.io, published 2026-10-14
  miter checkout: HEAD 2c6f9b0, tag v0.1.0-beta.4 at 17f9515, 87 commits ahead of the tag
  `miter deps` is absent from the tag and therefore absent from the published crate:
    git cat-file -e v0.1.0-beta.4:src/cli/args_deps.rs  ->  ABSENT in tag
  chalkline-cli 0.1.0-beta.4, published 2026-10-22; checkout HEAD 3b5253f, 52 commits ahead of its tag

THE STRUCTURAL PART, WHICH MATTERS MORE
A pinned git install is the obvious fallback and it does not work. miter's workspace resolves
`gaugeblock-security` by relative path into the *sibling* `common` repository, so a clone of miter
alone cannot load its own manifests:

  cargo install --git https://github.com/gaugeblock/miter --rev 2c6f9b0586d971ce9f825fa048f14d8f5746f996 \
    --locked miter-cli
  error: failed to load manifest for workspace member .../crates/engine
  Caused by: failed to read /Users/.../git/checkouts/miter-.../2c6f9b0/common/crates/gaugeblock-security/Cargo.toml
  Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)

So each tool is self-contained only as a published package: publishing flattens the path dependency
into a registry version, and cloning does not. Note the grep that misses this: neither miter/Cargo.toml
nor the member manifests show a `../` path at the site of use, because it is declared once in
[workspace.dependencies] and consumed with `workspace = true`.

WHY IT COSTS A CONSUMER
The suite documents gates (AGENTS.md §3.6 in a consumer: `miter audit`, `miter deps --unused`,
`chalkline docs check`) and cannot supply the tool that implements one of them. The consumer's choice
is: pin an older registry release and drop `miter deps` from CI, or build from a local checkout that
CI does not have. aerofoil pinned 0.1.0-beta.4, runs audit and docs check, and left `miter deps` as a
local-only gate — with the omission named in its workflow and its AGENTS.md §7 so it cannot read as
coverage.

WHAT CLOSES THIS
Either or both:
  * cut a release containing every command the documented tiers name, and keep the tag, the published
    crate and the checkout in step (the tag is what `git cat-file` and `cargo install --git --rev`
    would be pinned to, so a stale tag is itself a defect);
  * make the repositories installable from a clone, by publishing gaugeblock-security (and any other
    cross-repo path dependency) and depending on it by version, so `cargo install --git ... --rev`
    resolves without the sibling checkouts.

Acceptance for this ticket is the second one proven from a clean machine: the command above, verbatim,
completes and leaves a `miter` that answers `miter deps --unused`.

NOT IN SCOPE
Changing what any gate checks. This is about the same code being obtainable at the version a consumer
is told to run.
acceptance_criteria: cargo install --git https://github.com/gaugeblock/miter --rev <sha> --locked miter-cli succeeds from a clean machine with no sibling checkouts
the installed binary answers miter deps --unused
the tag, the published crate and the checkout carry the same commands, so a consumer pinning the tag gets the gate the documentation names
